mainTopic: The practices of אבוה דשמואל and the debate over rainwater in the פרת; אביי on fastening a cloak on a coin and on a nut as a trick; the new משנה about an amputee's wooden leg.
overview: This amud opens at the end of a proof. The גמרא tried to show from the practice of אבוה דשמואל, who kept his daughters from sleeping together, that רב הונא was right that women intimate with each other are פסולות לכהונה. The גמרא rejects that proof: he may only have wanted them not to get used to another body. His second practice, building a מקוה in ניסן, supports רב's view that the swelling of the פרת comes from rain, since rainwater does not purify while flowing. The גמרא notes that this argues with שמואל, and that שמואל's own two statements seem to clash. It then returns to the משנה. אביי explains that the rule against fastening a cloak לכתחילה on שבת refers only to a coin, which is מוקצה. אביי then asks whether a woman may fasten her cloak on a nut as a trick (הערמה) to carry it to her child, comparing it to the trick allowed in a fire. The question ends with תיקו. Finally, a new משנה begins: רבי מאיר says an amputee may go out on שבת with his wooden leg.

steps.title: Finishing the proof from רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: This amud opens with the last words of רב הונא's ruling. The גמרא is using that ruling to explain why אבוה דשמואל kept his daughters from sleeping together.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the closing words of a proof that started on the previous amud. The full ruling of רב הונא is that women who are intimate with each other are פסולות לכהונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wanted to say that אבוה דשמואל separated his daughters so they would not become disqualified from marrying a כהן. If that were his reason, his practice would support רב הונא's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Disqualified
The priesthood (here: marrying a כהן)
Women intimate with one another (from the earlier part of the sentence)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new statement. It is the tail end of a sentence that began on the previous section, quoting רב הונא.

phrases.english: are disqualified from the priesthood.
phrases.notes: This finishes רב הונא's ruling, brought here as a possible reason for what אבוה דשמואל did.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a proof attempt that began on the previous amud.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's ruling that women intimate with each other are disqualified from כהונה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of אבוה דשמואל not letting his daughters sleep together

steps.title: Rejecting the proof with a different reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the practice does not prove רב הונא's ruling. אבוה דשמואל may simply have wanted his daughters not to get used to sleeping next to another body.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. He thought: so that they should not become used to a foreign body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It offers another possible reason for the father's practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father may not have held that such intimacy disqualifies a woman from כהונה at all. He may only have been worried that getting used to another person's body would awaken desire. Since his practice can be explained without רב הונא's ruling, it proves nothing about that ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: No (the proof is rejected)
So that ... not
They should become accustomed / learn
A foreign body (another person's body)

phrases.english: No — he held
so that they would not become accustomed
to a foreign body.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא — סָבַר כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא לֵילְפָן גּוּפָא נוּכְרָאָה
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not reject רב הונא's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The practice can be explained by a separate concern about desire, so it does not depend on רב הונא's ruling.

steps.title: The מקוה in ניסן supports רב
steps.stepSummary: אבוה דשמואל built his daughters a מקוה in ניסן instead of having them immerse in the river. This supports רב, who said the swelling of the פרת is a sign of rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he made a מקוה for them in the days of ניסן. This supports רב, for רב said: rain in the West, the great witness is the פרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a second practice of the father. It shows that this practice supports רב's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said that when rain falls in ארץ ישראל ("the West"), the rising פרת testifies to it. In other words, the river's growth comes from rainwater. That fits the father's refusal to rely on the river in ניסן, right after the rainy season.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritual bath of gathered water
The spring month, right after the rains
This supports him
Rain in the West (ארץ ישראל)
The great witness is the פרת (Euphrates)

phrases.english: And he made a ritual bath for them in the days of Nisan,
this supports Rav,
as Rav said:
rain in the West —
the great witness is the Euphrates.
phrases.notes: The swelling of the river shows that rain fell.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the sleeping practice to the father's מקוה practice.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that the increase of the פרת comes from rainwater
steps.raayaSupportSource: אבוה דשמואל built a מקוה in ניסן rather than relying on the river

steps.title: Why the father did not trust the river in ניסן
steps.stepSummary: The father was concerned that in ניסן the rainwater (נוטפין) would outweigh the river's own flowing water (זוחלין).
steps.simpleTranslation: He held: so that the dripping waters should not be more than the flowing waters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the father's reasoning. This explains why his practice matches רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Flowing water purifies only if it is natural spring or river water. Rainwater purifies only when it is gathered and still. In ניסן, rain might make up most of the river, so immersing in the flowing river might not purify, and he built a stationary מקוה instead.

keyTerms.meaning: Dripping waters (rainwater)
Flowing waters (spring or river water)
That they should not be more than

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the basic rule behind the rest of this passage: rainwater does not purify while it flows, but spring water does.

phrases.english: He held: that there should not be more
dripping waters than flowing waters.
phrases.notes: Rainwater must not outnumber the river's natural water.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר, שֶׁלֹּא יִרְבּוּ הַנּוֹטְפִין עַל הַזּוֹחֲלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the practice cited in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A river purifies by flowing only if rainwater does not outweigh its natural water.

steps.title: This argues with שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the father's view argues with his son שמואל. שמואל said a river's growth comes from its own bed, not from rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it argues with שמואל, for שמואל said: a river is blessed from its own bed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that שמואל holds the opposite view about where a river's extra water comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to שמואל, the extra water in a river comes up from underground sources in its bed. On that view a river is always natural flowing water, even in ניסן. So there would be no reason to avoid it, unlike what the father and רב hold.

keyTerms.meaning: And it argues with
A river
From its bed/banks (its own source)
Is blessed (increases)

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Shmuel.
As Shmuel said:
A river is blessed from its own bed.
phrases.notes: The increase comes from underground, not from rain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents an opposing view to the one in steps 3-4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל: a river's increase comes from its own source, so its water stays natural flowing water.

steps.title: שמואל seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: שמואל also said flowing water purifies only in the פרת during תשרי. That implies rain does affect the river, which clashes with his statement in step 5.
steps.simpleTranslation: And his own words contradict his own words, for שמואל said: water purifies when flowing only in the פרת in the days of תשרי alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that שמואל's two statements seem to clash. It only notes the contradiction and does not resolve it. The next step returns to the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a river is always fed from its bed, it should purify all year. Limiting it to תשרי, the end of the dry summer, suggests that at other times rainwater is mixed in. So the second statement seems to agree with רב, against שמואל's first statement.

keyTerms.meaning: His own statement against his own statement
Purify
The autumn month, after the dry summer
Only, alone

steps.whatToRemember: רב (and the father): a swollen river is rainwater, so don't rely on it in ניסן. שמואל in one place: a river grows from its own bed. שמואל in another place: flowing water purifies only in the פרת in תשרי. The last two seem to contradict.

phrases.english: And his own statement disagrees with his own statement,
as Shmuel said:
Water does not purify when flowing
except the Euphrates
in the days of Tishrei alone.
phrases.notes: After the dry summer, the river is clearly its own water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out a contradiction between שמואל's statement in step 5 and another statement of his.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's statement that a river is blessed from its own bed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a river's water always comes from its own source, it should purify all year. Limiting it to תשרי implies that rain affects the river at other times.

steps.title: The משנה seems to contradict itself about fastening on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about fastening a cloak on a stone. It points out that the first part says she may fasten, which sounds fully permitted. The last part says she may not fasten it לכתחילה on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'She may fasten her cloak on a stone, etc.' But didn't you say in the first part 'she may fasten'? So how can the end say she may not fasten it on שבת לכתחילה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and points out an apparent contradiction between its beginning and its end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause, 'פורפת', sounds like she may fasten even on שבת itself. The final clause, 'ובלבד שלא תפרוף לכתחילה בשבת', seems to forbid exactly that. The גמרא wants to know which ruling is true.

keyTerms.meaning: She fastens (wraps a corner of her cloak around a small object to tie it)
The first part of a משנה or ברייתא
But didn't you say? (introduces an internal contradiction)
Etc. (the rest of the quoted text)

steps.confusionAlert: This is a jump back to the משנה. The earlier discussion about אבוה דשמואל and the river was a side topic. Now we are back on the cloak-fastening line of the משנה.

phrases.english: [The Mishnah:] She may fasten [her cloak] on a stone, etc.
phrases.notes: The full line in the משנה ends: 'as long as she does not fasten it לכתחילה on שבת.'

phrases.english: But didn't you say in the first clause 'she may fasten'?
phrases.notes: The first clause sounds fully permitted, yet the end limits it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about rivers and מקוה and returns to the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the משנה: 'פורפת' versus 'ובלבד שלא תפרוף לכתחילה בשבת'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The opening permits fastening, but the closing forbids fastening לכתחילה on שבת. The same משנה cannot say both about the same case.

steps.title: The limiting clause refers only to the coin
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the end of the משנה is talking only about a coin. Stones and nuts may be fastened even on שבת. A coin is מוקצה, so it may not be fastened לכתחילה on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The last part of the משנה is talking about the coin.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction by saying the two parts of the משנה refer to different objects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'She may fasten' applies to the stone and the nut, even on שבת. 'Not לכתחילה on שבת' applies only to the coin, because a coin is מוקצה and may not be handled on שבת. If she fastened it before שבת, she may go out with it.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה or ברייתא
We have come to (now the text is discussing...)
A coin (מוקצה on שבת)
An object set aside from use, which may not be handled on שבת

phrases.english: Abaye said:
In the latter clause we have arrived at the coin.
phrases.notes: Only the coin may not be fastened לכתחילה on שבת, because it is מוקצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the two clauses refer to different objects.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses seemed to refer to all three objects, which made them contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Stone and nut may be fastened even on שבת. Only the coin, which is מוקצה, is limited to being fastened before שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: Stone and nut may be fastened even on שבת. A coin may not be fastened לכתחילה on שבת because it is מוקצה.

steps.title: May a woman use a trick to carry a nut out to her child?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks a new question. May a woman fasten her cloak around a nut, which is normally allowed, when her real goal is to bring the nut out to her small child in the public domain on שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי asked: May a woman use a trick, fastening her cloak on a nut, in order to bring it out to her young son on שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks a question (בעיא): does the permission to fasten on a nut still apply when it is used as a trick to carry the nut for her child?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fastening on a nut is allowed because the nut is serving the cloak. Here, though, her real intent is to carry the nut itself to her child. The question is whether this הערמה (trick) is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (raises a dilemma)
What is the law?
That she uses a trick (from הערמה)
Nut

phrases.english: Abaye raised a dilemma:
A woman, what is [the law] that she employ a trick
and fasten [her cloak] on a nut
in order to take it out to her young son on Shabbat?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the permission to fasten on a nut and asks about using it as a trick.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether fastening on a nut is permitted when the real goal is to carry the nut out for a child.

steps.title: The question applies to both sides of the dispute about tricks
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that אביי's question is open according to both opinions. It applies to the view that allows tricks and to the view that forbids tricks.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a question according to the one who says we may use a trick, and it is a question according to the one who says we may not use a trick.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It states that the question exists under both opinions, and then it will explain why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known dispute about using tricks on שבת in the case of a fire: wearing many layers of clothing to rescue them from a burning house. The גמרא says אביי's question cannot be settled simply by picking a side in that dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be asked (the question applies)
We may use a trick
We may not use a trick

phrases.english: It is a question according to the one who says one may employ a trick.
It is a question according to the one who says one may not employ a trick.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Frames אביי's question against the known dispute about tricks.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי's question is open under both views on הערמה.

steps.title: Why even the lenient view might forbid this trick
steps.stepSummary: Even the view that allows tricks during a fire may not allow this one. In a fire, if we forbid the trick, the person might put out the fire. Here, if we forbid the trick, she will simply not take the nut out.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a question even according to the one who allows a trick in a fire. There, if you don't allow him, he may come to put out the fire. But here, if you don't allow her, she will not come to carry it out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the lenient view on fire does not automatically decide אביי's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a fire, the trick is allowed to prevent a worse sin: extinguishing the fire. With the nut there is no such danger, because the woman will not carry it out illegally. So the reason for leniency may not apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: A fire
You permit
To extinguish
To carry out

steps.confusionAlert: The fire case is allowed because of a fear of something worse (extinguishing). It is not a general permission to use tricks whenever we like.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a leniency for tricks depends on its reason. A trick allowed to prevent a bigger violation may not be allowed when no such risk exists.

phrases.english: It is a question according to the one who says one may employ a trick in a fire:

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם הוּא דְּאִי לָא שָׁרֵית לֵיהּ
phrases.english: There it is [allowed] because if you do not permit him
phrases.notes: To wear the clothing out of the burning house.

phrases.english: he will come to extinguish [the fire],

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא אִי לָא שָׁרֵית לֵיהּ
phrases.english: but here, if you do not permit her
she will not come to carry it out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of step 10: why the lenient view still has a question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leniency for tricks in a fire rests on the fear of extinguishing. That fear is missing in the nut case, so the leniency may not apply.

steps.title: The other side: even the strict view might allow the nut
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the opposite way of looking at אביי's question. Even the view that forbids tricks during a fire might allow this trick, because using a nut as a button is not a normal way of carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe, even according to the one who says we may not use tricks during a fire, there is a difference. There, wearing clothes is the normal way to carry clothes out. But here, fastening a nut into a cloak is not the normal way to carry a nut out. So say that it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 11 gave one side: even the lenient view might forbid the nut trick. Now the גמרא gives the other side: even the strict view might permit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a fire, putting on extra clothes is the normal way to carry clothes, so the trick comes very close to real carrying. Fastening a nut into a cloak is not a normal way to carry a nut, so it is at most a smaller, rabbinic problem. For that reason, even the strict view might allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps. This introduces the other side of a question.
Using a trick to get around a prohibition
A fire, specifically a fire on שבת
The normal way of carrying something out
It is fine. It is permitted.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two sides. Step 11 said even the lenient view might forbid the nut trick. This step says even the strict view might permit it. These are the two sides of one open question.

phrases.english: Or perhaps,
even according to the one who says
one may not use tricks in the case of a fire,
there, this is the normal way of carrying out,
phrases.notes: Wearing garments is how people normally carry clothing.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא — אֵין דֶּרֶךְ הוֹצָאָה בְּכָךְ,
phrases.english: but here, this is not the normal way of carrying out,
phrases.notes: A nut used as a button is not how people carry nuts.

phrases.english: say that it is fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא, אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין מַעֲרִימִין בִּדְלֵיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side of the question laid out in step 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Possibly permitted even by the strict view, because a nut used as a button is not a normal way of carrying

steps.title: The question is left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends אביי's question with תיקו. It does not decide whether the nut trick is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot decide between the two sides, so it closes the discussion without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides were reasonable. The comparison to the fire case could point either way, so no ruling comes out of it.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand. The question remains unresolved.

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's question about fastening a cloak around a nut in order to carry the nut to a child stays open. One side says even the lenient view forbids it, because she will simply not take the nut out. The other side says even the strict view allows it, because this is not a normal way of carrying.

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question opened in step 9 without resolving it

steps.title: New משנה: an amputee may go out with his wooden leg
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. A person with an amputated leg may go out on שבת with his wooden leg, according to רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A person with an amputated leg may go out on שבת with his wooden leg. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new משנה about what a person may wear when going out on שבת. Only רבי מאיר's opinion appears here, so another view is about to follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר treats the wooden leg like a shoe, something the person wears. So going out with it is not carrying. The phrase דברי רבי מאיר signals that a disagreeing opinion comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. This marks the start of a new משנה.
A person with an amputated leg
A wooden leg or stump support
These are the words of רבי מאיר. This signals that someone may disagree.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One with an amputated leg may go out with his wooden leg,
phrases.notes: It is treated like a shoe.

phrases.english: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה after the previous discussion was closed with תיקו
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, an amputee may go out on שבת with his wooden leg.
